sections.name: THE EASTERN DISTRICT OF PENNSYLVANIA
sentences: ________________________________ West Chester, PA 19382 : CIVIL ACTION NO. TOWER HEALTH : JURY TRIAL DEMANDED.

sections.name: INTRODUCTION
sentences: Plaintiff, Danielle Lynch Nicholson, brings this action against her former employer Tower Health and one of its subsidiaries, Reading Hospital (“Defendants”).
Defendant terminated Plaintiff shortly after she advised that she was pregnant and failed to place her into open positions for which she was qualified.

Defendants’ unlawful conduct towards Plaintiff violated Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, as amended, 42 U.S.C. § 2000e, et seq. (“Title VII”), and the Pennsylvania Human Relations Act, as amended, 43 P.S. § 951, et seq. (“PHRA”).

sections.name: PARTIES
sentences: Plaintiff, Danielle Lynch Nicholson, is an individual and a citizen of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.
She resides in West Chester, PA 19382.
Defendant, Tower Health, is an entity with a principal place of business at 420 S. Fifth Avenue West, Reading, PA 19611.
Defendant, Reading Hospital, is an entity with a principal place of business at 420 S. Fifth Avenue, West Reading, PA 19611.

The website for Defendant Tower Health states that it is a “strong, regional, integrated healthcare provider/payer system that offers leading-edge, compassionate healthcare and wellness services to a population of 2.5 million people.” Plaintiff’s email address during her employment with Defendant was danielle.lynch@towerhealth.org.
Defendants are engaged in an industry affecting interstate commerce and regularly do business in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania.
At all times material hereto, Defendants employed more than fifteen (15) employees.

At all times material hereto, Defendants acted by and through their authorized agents, servants, workmen, and/or employees acting within the course and scope of their employment with Defendants and in furtherance of Defendants’ business.
At all times material hereto, Defendants acted as employers within the meaning of the statutes which form the basis of this matter.
At all times material hereto, Plaintiff was an employee of Defendants within the meaning of the statutes which form the basis of this matter.

sections.name: JURISDICTION AND VENUE
sentences: The causes of action which form the basis of this matter arise under Title VII and the PHRA.
The District Court has jurisdiction over Count I (Title VII) pursuant to 42 S.C. § 2000e-5 and 28 U.S.C. § 1331.
The District Court has supplemental jurisdiction over Count II (PHRA) pursuant to 28 U.S.C. §1367.
Venue is proper in the District Court under 28 U.S.C. §1391(b) and 42 S.C. §2000(e)-5(f).
On or about March 17, 2021, Plaintiff filed a Complaint with the PHRC, complaining of acts of discrimination alleged herein.
Her Complaint was cross-filed with the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (“EEOC”).
Attached hereto, incorporated herein and marked as Exhibit “1” is a true and correct copy of the PHRC Complaint (with personal identifying information redacted).
On or about August 16, 2022, the EEOC issued to Plaintiff a Dismissal and Notice of Rights for her PHRC Complaint.
Attached hereto, incorporated herein and marked as Exhibit “2” is a true and correct copy of that notice (with personal identifying information redacted).
Plaintiff has fully complied with all administrative prerequisites for the commencement of this action.

sections.name: FACTUAL ALLEGATIONS
sentences: Plaintiff commenced her employment with Defendant Tower Health on or about December 2, 2019.
Plaintiff was hired into the position of Marketing Coordinator at Brandywine Hospital, which was part of Defendant Tower Health.
She held that position throughout her employment.
As part of Plaintiff’s job responsibilities, she was part of Defendant Tower Health’s Social Media Team which consisted of Marketing employees from hospitals throughout the health system.
Plaintiff consistently performed her job duties in a highly competent manner and received positive feedback regarding the same.
As of the time that Defendant Tower Health terminated Plaintiff’s employment, she reported directly to James Gechter, Web/Social Media Content Manager, and Mary Beth Lowery, Marketing Director.
Gechter reported to Kimberly Slattery, System Director, Web Services.

Lowery reported to Lisa Hess (female), Vice President, Marketing and Corporate Communications for Defendant Tower Health, and Claire Mooney, President and Chief Executive Officer, Brandywine Hospital.
On or about January 11, 2021, Plaintiff learned that she was pregnant and due on September 14, 2021.
Plaintiff advised Defendants, through a phone call with Gechter, of her pregnancy on or about January 14, 2021.

During her call with Gechter, Plaintiff expressed concern about working in-person at the office, as there was then a surge of Covid-19 cases and her doctor had advised against her getting the Covid vaccine due to her pregnancy.
Plaintiff told Gechter that she knew that Lowery was pushing for employees to return to in-person work.
Plaintiff also told Gechter that her due date was mid-September 2021.

On or about January 19, 2021, Plaintiff also advised Lowery that she was pregnant and that, due to the same and her doctor’s medical advice not to receive the vaccine and the then-current Covid-19 case surge, she was concerned about working in- person at the office.

Plaintiff also expressed to Lowery that she had been waiting a long time to become a mother and how significant her pregnancy was to her. Plaintiff also told Lowery that she had been feeling more tired than usual due to her pregnancy.
Lowery told Plaintiff that her pregnancy was bad timing.
Lowery also asked Plaintiff how far along she was in her pregnancy and when her due date was. Plaintiff told her that her due date was in mid-September.
Lowery told Plaintiff that it would be interesting to see what happened next.
Lowery also said that she was not certain how Mooney would react if she heard that Plaintiff was pregnant.
Following Plaintiff’s conversation with Lowery, Plaintiff advised Gechter that she had told Lowery of her pregnancy.

Plaintiff also told Gechter that she had a pregnancy-related doctor’s appointment later that month for which she would need to take paid time off. On or about January 29, 2021, Plaintiff submitted a doctor’s note requesting that she be permitted to work from home as an accommodation for her pregnancy.
Plaintiff subsequently advised Lowery of her doctor’s note and accommodation request.
Lowery asked Plaintiff if she needed to work from home during the entirety of her pregnancy or whether she would be able to re-evaluate her accommodation request at her next doctor’s appointment.
Lowery also asked Plaintiff when she planned to get the Covid vaccine.
Plaintiff told Lowery that she would follow her doctor’s recommendations and medical advice.
Plaintiff also told Lowery that her doctor recommended that she wait until her second trimester to get the vaccine.
Lowery told Plaintiff that it was hard for her to plan when she did not have a lot of information from Plaintiff.
Defendants approved Plaintiff’s request to work from home due to her pregnancy.
Shortly thereafter, Gechter asked Plaintiff if Defendant had approved her accommodation request.
Plaintiff confirmed that her request had been approved.

After Plaintiff informed Defendants of her pregnancy and after she submitted a request for an accommodation in connection with the same, Defendants treated her worse than she had prior to her pregnancy, as set forth herein.
After Plaintiff advised of her pregnancy, Lowery and Gechter did not assign Plaintiff as many new projects/tasks as they had previously.
After Plaintiff advised of her pregnancy, Lowery and Gechter removed certain job duties and responsibilities from Plaintiff.
After Plaintiff advised of her pregnancy, Lowery reduced her communications with Plaintiff.
After Plaintiff advised of her pregnancy, Lowery ignored Plaintiff’s requests for additional work.

After Plaintiff advised of her pregnancy, Lowery excluded Plaintiff from certain communications related to Plaintiff’s job responsibilities and did not provide Plaintiff with certain information that Plaintiff needed to perform her job. After Plaintiff advised of her pregnancy, Lowery excluded Plaintiff from projects for which she had previously asked for Plaintiff’s assistance.
On or about February 13, 2021, Plaintiff applied for a Marketing Specialist position at Defendant Reading Hospital.
Defendant Reading Hospital was part of Defendant Tower Health.
Plaintiff was qualified for the position of Marketing Specialist at Defendant Reading Hospital.
On or about February 15, 2021, Gechter advised that Defendants had hired another Marketing Coordinator at Defendant Reading Hospital.
Gechter said that the new Marketing Coordinator would be assigned one of Plaintiff’s job responsibilities.

That job responsibility that Defendants removed from Plaintiff and assigned to the new Marketing Coordinator was a significant part of Plaintiff’s job. On or about February 17, 2021, Defendants informed Plaintiff that her employment was terminated, effective immediately.
Plaintiff was told that her employment was being terminated because her position was being eliminated.
Plaintiff was also told that her termination was not a result of poor performance.
Plaintiff was the only employee who reported to Lowery and Gechter who was terminated effective February 17, 2021.
Defendants did not offer Plaintiff any opportunity to remain employed at that time.
There were open positions for which Plaintiff was qualified as of the time of her termination.

On or about February 22, 2021, Plaintiff interviewed with Chrystal Schardt, Interim Marketing Director at Defendant Reading Hospital, for the Marketing Specialist position for which she had previously applied.
On or about February 24, 2021, Defendant advised Plaintiff that she had not been selected for the Marketing Specialist position at Reading Hospital.
Defendant did not provide Plaintiff with a reason as to why she was not selected for the Marketing Specialist position.
On or about March 1, 2021, Plaintiff interviewed for an open Corporate Communications Manager at Reading Hospital.
Plaintiff was qualified for the position of Corporate Communications Manager.
Defendants did not hire Plaintiff for the position of Corporate Communications Manager.

In around late March 2021, Defendants advised Plaintiff that it put the Corporate Communications Manager position on hold while it evaluated positions and that it would get in touch with her if it were re-opened.
No one at Defendants got back to Plaintiff about the Corporate Communications Manager position or any other open position at Defendants.

Plaintiff’s pregnancy was a motivating and/or determinative factor in Defendants’ discriminatory treatment of Plaintiff, including terminating her employment, failing to place her into the Marketing Specialist position, and failing to place her into the Corporate Communications Manager position.
Defendants failed to prevent or address the discriminatory conduct referred to herein and further failed to take corrective and remedial measures to make the workplace free of discriminatory conduct.

As a direct and proximate result of the discriminatory conduct of Defendants, Plaintiff has in the past incurred, and may in the future incur, a loss of earnings and/or earning capacity, loss of benefits, pain and suffering, embarrassment, humiliation, loss of self-esteem, mental anguish, and loss of life’s pleasures, the full extent of which is not known at this time.
The conduct of Defendant, as set forth above, was outrageous under the circumstances and warrants the imposition of punitive damages against Defendant.

sections.name: COUNT I – Title VII
sentences: Plaintiff incorporates herein by reference paragraphs 1 through 70 above, as if set forth herein in their entirety.

By committing the foregoing acts of discrimination against Plaintiff, Defendants have violated Title VII. Defendant acted intentionally, and with malice and/or reckless indifference to Plaintiff’s rights, and its conduct warrants the imposition of punitive damages.
As a direct and proximate result of Defendants’ violation of Title VII, Plaintiff has suffered the damages and losses set forth herein and has incurred attorney’s fees and costs.

Plaintiff is now suffering and will continue to suffer irreparable injury and monetary damages as a result of Defendants’ discriminatory acts unless and until this Court grants the relief requested herein.
No previous application has been made for the relief requested herein.

sections.name: COUNT II – PHRA
sentences: Plaintiff incorporates herein by reference paragraphs 1 through 76 above, as if set forth herein in their entirety.
Defendants, by the above improper and discriminatory acts, have violated the PHRA.
Said violations were intentional and willful.
As a direct and proximate result of Defendants’ violation of the PHRA, Plaintiff has sustained the injuries, damages, and losses set forth herein and has incurred attorney’s fees and costs.

Plaintiff is now suffering and will continue to suffer irreparable injuries and monetary damages as a result of Defendants’ discriminatory acts unless and until the Court grants the relief requested herein.
No previous application has been made for the relief requested herein.

WHEREFORE, Plaintiff seeks damages and legal and equitable relief in connection with Defendants’ improper conduct, and specifically prays that the Court grant the following relief to the Plaintiff by: (a) declaring the acts and practices complained of herein to be in.

sections.name: violation of Title VII;
sentences: (b) declaring the acts and practices complained of herein to be in violation of the PHRA; (c) enjoining and permanently restraining the violations alleged herein; (d) entering judgment against the Defendants and in favor of the Plaintiff in an amount to be determined; (e) awarding compensatory damages to make the Plaintiff whole for all lost earnings, earning capacity and benefits, past and future, which Plaintiff has suffered or may suffer as a result of Defendants’ improper conduct; (f) awarding compensatory damages to Plaintiff for past and future pain and suffering, emotional upset, mental anguish, humiliation, and loss of life’s pleasures, which Plaintiff has suffered or may suffer as a result of Defendants’ improper conduct; (g) awarding punitive damages to Plaintiff under Title VII; (h) awarding Plaintiff such other damages as are appropriate under Title VII and the PHRA; (i) awarding Plaintiff the costs of suit, expert fees and other disbursements, and reasonable attorney’s fees; and, (j) granting such other and further relief as this Court may deem just, proper, or equitable including other equitable and injunctive relief providing restitution for past violations and preventing future violations.
